checks.name: BEE-NET model weights (Hennig group; Gibson et al., arXiv 2503.20005 / npj Comput Mater 2026)
checks.url_checked: https://huggingface.co/paprakash/BEE-NET (file listing and README via hf_fs, card via hub_repo_details); https://huggingface.co/datasets/paprakash/BEE-NET_data (README and listing); https://github.com/henniggroup/BEE-NET and .../tree/main/workflow (WebFetch); arXiv 2503.20005v2 full text (alphaXiv); OpenAlex record for 10.1038/s41524-026-01964-8
checks.access_verified: [Certain] Both Hugging Face repos are public and ungated. The model repo holds 100 CSO and 100 CPD checkpoints plus database.json. The dataset repo holds the same database.json, 5,241 CIFs, 200 bootstrap train/val index pairs and a 1,049-ID test split. [Certain] The GitHub repo is public and has notebooks, workflow scripts (M3GNet relax, MEGNet, BEE-NET prediction, QE helpers) and the training structures. Nothing was downloaded because of size.
checks.license_verified: [Certain] Neither the HF model card nor the dataset card declares a licence. [Likely] The GitHub README shows none either (WebFetch summary). The paper itself is CC BY-NC-ND (OpenAlex). The training data come from the Cerqueira-Sanna-Marques Materials Cloud archive, which is CC BY 4.0. Treat the weights as unlicensed until the authors say otherwise.
checks.size_verified: [Certain] The CPD checkpoints are 60,676,697 bytes each and the CSO checkpoints 60,650,585 bytes each, so each variant is about 6.07 GB and the pair about 12.1 GB. The entry's 'about 60 MB per model' is per ensemble member, not per variant. database.json is 449,282,758 bytes and holds 5,241 entries. [Certain] The dataset README says the paper's '~7,000' spectra are the source pool and BEE-NET uses 5,241 of them. [Certain] Test metrics: CPD-EMD Tc MAE 0.87 K (R2 0.79), CSO-EMD 1.20 K, TNR 0.994 (CPD-MSE) for Tc <= 5 K. The screen went from 1.3M structures to 866 DFT alpha2F runs and 741 compounds with Tc > 5 K, 69 of them at or above 20 K.
checks.label_quality: Calculated only. Targets are alpha2F from QE PBEsol harmonic isotropic DFPT (Cerqueira et al.), turned into Tc with Allen-Dynes. The model covers alpha2F only up to 100 meV and was trained only on ambient-pressure data. [Certain] The authors say it is unlikely to predict hydride-like high Tc. Only two compounds were checked against measurement: Be2Hf2Nb (resistive onset 3.18 K measured; 14.9 K at the screening calculation, 9.3 K recalculated with mu*=0.21) and Be2HfNb2 (4.24 K measured; 7.5 K and 5.1 K calculated; the sample had several phases with two specific-heat jumps). In both cases the calculated Tc was higher than the measured one.
checks.hpc_candidate: Be2Hf2Nb and Be2HfNb2 are Hf substitutions in the U3Si2-type Be2Nb3 structure (P4/mbm; Hf on the 2a or 4h Nb sites). Calculated Tc (QE PBEsol DFPT, harmonic, Allen-Dynes): 14.9 K and 7.5 K at screening; 9.3 K and 5.1 K at mu*=0.21. E_hull is 94 and 62 meV/atom (VASP), so both are metastable. Both have already been made by arc melting and measured, with onsets of 3.18 K and 4.24 K, RRR about 1, and refined Hf/Nb site disorder (Be2Hf2Nb: Hf:Nb 87.5:12.5 on 2a and 56.25:43.75 on 4h). I did not find a full refined CIF; the occupancies are in the SM. They are not worth HPC time for the room-temperature goal. The 741-compound list (69 with calculated Tc >= 20 K) is not released as a file. [Certain] It is absent from both HF repos. [Likely] The GitHub README and workflow folder do not have it either; the folder holds only notebooks, scripts and test.pkl.
checks.why: The weights and their two headline numbers are real and open to download. Two parts of the entry are wrong or incomplete. First, the model is about 12 GB, not 60 MB. Second, the data inside the repo (5,241 Cerqueira-Sanna-Marques alpha2F entries) come from the same Materials Cloud archive (3kbt5-r3n56) as the project's 8,203 Alexandria rows (docs/physics-proxy2.md), so they are mostly duplicates. The only new piece is a structure-based predictor of lambda, omega_log and Tc. It cannot feed the composition-only ranker directly. The project's own test found that calculated electron-phonon proxies did not help predict experimental labels (docs/data-sources.md, physics-proxy2 P1b). For the room-temperature goal, the authors themselves say the model cannot see hydride-like high-Tc spectra. The useful part, the 741-compound list and its 69 entries at or above 20 K, has not been published.
checks.next_step: Do not download the 12 GB ensembles. Ask the corresponding authors for (a) the 741 DFT-confirmed compounds with structures, E_hull and calculated Tc, and (b) a licence for the weights. If the list arrives, triage its 69 entries at or above 20 K as HPC candidates. Scoring project structures with one CSO checkpoint (about 61 MB, over the 20 MB sample limit) needs the owner's approval first.

checks.name: Gao et al. 20,000+ metal e-ph set: bulk route through the Alexandria site's superconductor folder
checks.url_checked: https://alexandria.icams.rub.de/data/older/supercon_dataset/README.txt (curl 200, 1,663 bytes) and its folder listing; https://alexandria.icams.rub.de/datasets.html and about.html; https://alexandria.icams.rub.de/data/pbesol_ph/3d/ (listing), /3d/2024.07.10/ and /2d/; byte-range samples (5-6 MB) of alexandria_ph_000, _020 and _092.json.bz2, decompressed with python -I; https://archive.materialscloud.org/api/records/3kbt5-r3n56; OpenAlex records for 10.1038/s41467-025-63702-w and 10.1002/adfm.202404043; arXiv 2502.18281 with SI (alphaXiv); arXiv 2604.12367 (alphaXiv)
checks.access_verified: [Certain] The directory listings are open plain HTTPS with no login, and curl reaches them from this session. Only WebFetch fails on this host (DNS), which explains the swarm's 'not reachable'. [Certain] data/older/supercon_dataset/ holds only the raw QE batches of Cerqueira, Sanna and Marques (Adv. Mater.): 17 tar.bz2 files of about 51 GB. They are byte-for-byte the same 17 files and sizes as Materials Cloud 3kbt5-r3n56, which is the project's existing source. [Certain] The newer folder the entry guessed at exists. datasets.html links 'Phonon & electron-phonon (Quantum Espresso) 2025.08.11' to data/pbesol_ph/3d/ and /2d/, citing 10.1002/adfm.202404043 (the hydride paper).
checks.license_verified: [Certain] alexandria.icams.rub.de/about.html says Alexandria is under CC BY 4.0. The 3kbt5 Materials Cloud record is also CC BY 4.0, and the Gao et al. article is CC BY.
checks.size_verified: [Certain] The 2025.08.11 3D release has 93 files (alexandria_ph_000 to 092.json.bz2), 5.06 GB compressed in total. The 2D release has 4 files (about 0.2 GB). The earlier 3D release (2024.07.10) has 34 files, 1.73 GB. [Certain] Each record is a pymatgen ComputedStructureEntry with mat_id (agm...), formula, relaxed structure, k/q grids, dynamical matrices, an imag flag, a2F at several smearings and a tc block. The tc block holds lambda, wlog, w2av, a mu* grid from 0 to 0.38, TcMcMillan, TcAllenDynes and TcEliashberg; Tc is null when imag is true. Samples: in file 000 the first 904 entries were all imag=true with no Tc. File 020: 10 of 11 entries had Tc (B-C, Li/Na-B-C, H8Mg2Y). File 092: 14 of 23 had Tc (hydrides such as H4Al2, H8Cu3Sr, H12CaCu5, H8AlLi2Pd, and Nb nitrides). [Speculative] I did not count the entries that carry Tc because that needs all 5 GB; the total is plausibly the 'more than 20 000 metals' in Gao et al. One correction: the project holds 8,203 rows, not 8,253.
checks.label_quality: Calculated: QE PBEsol DFPT, harmonic, isotropic. Tc is given by McMillan, Allen-Dynes and isotropic Eliashberg over a mu* grid. The q-grids are coarse (3x3x3 to 4x4x4) and the fine k-grid is twice the coarse one (Gao SI, Certain). Dynamically unstable entries are flagged and carry no Tc. [Certain] Gao et al. state that the high-Tc entries are increasingly unstable thermodynamically, and that the harmonic phonons of the top hydride Li2AgH6 show small instabilities near Gamma. There are no measured labels and no 'not superconducting' results.
checks.hpc_candidate: All values below are calculated (QE PBEsol DFPT, harmonic unless noted), and none of these compounds has been made. Full primitive cells and Alexandria IDs are in the Gao et al. SI. (1) Li2AgH6 (agm006188332, Fm-3m): E_hull 0.319 eV/atom; lambda 3.78; Tc 66.5 K (McMillan), 110.6 K (Allen-Dynes), 132.3 K (Eliashberg). Recomputed with ab initio Coulomb interaction: 108.8 K (Eliashberg) and 83.0 K (SCDFT). SSCHA (anharmonic) removes the harmonic instability. (2) Li2AuH6 (Fm-3m): E_hull 0.172 eV/atom; 116.1 K (Eliashberg) and 91.0 K (SCDFT). Anharmonic SSCHA Allen-Dynes gives 107-118 K at mu*=0.1. [Certain] A path-integral MD study (Ding, Chen and Shi, arXiv 2604.12367) finds both compounds kinetically unstable at 80 K: Li2AgH6 collapses, and in Li2AuH6 hydrogen dimerises and diffuses, giving an SPIA Tc of 22 K. [Likely] A web search found no synthesis report for either. (3) Al2H7Os (agm006206343, Fm-3m): E_hull 0.265 eV/atom; lambda 3.18; 37.6 K (McMillan), 57.3 K (Allen-Dynes), 100 K (Eliashberg). (4) BC11 (agm006148322, space group 21): E_hull 0.225 eV/atom; 24.0 K (Eliashberg). (5) ClB2C8 (B-doped C clathrate): lambda about 3.3, Tc 55 K. Gao et al. also name the Pareto front near the hull: LiMoN2, Mo2Pr3N6, Mg2IrH6, Mg2RhH6 and KInH3.
checks.why: This is the most useful of my three entries. The swarm's guess was right. A newer, larger electron-phonon release sits on the same server under data/pbesol_ph/3d/ (2025.08.11), not under the supercon folder. It is open and CC BY 4.0, and the sampled records hold lambda, omega_log and three Tc formulas with full structures and dynamic-stability flags. Samples show it covers the ambient-pressure hydride and B-C sets the project lacks. The project's 8,203 rows came from the older 3kbt5 archive, so much of this release is probably new, though the exact overlap is unmeasured until the agm IDs are compared. It is unlikely to improve the composition-only ranker, which already found calculated proxies did not transfer to experiment. It is the best open source of calculated ambient-pressure high-Tc hydride and boron-carbide structures for choosing HPC candidates, but its own authors conclude that conventional superconductivity at room temperature and ambient pressure is 'extremely unlikely'.
checks.next_step: With the owner's approval (5.06 GB is above the sample limit), stream the 93 files into the git-ignored data/raw/ area. Parse them with a streaming JSON reader and keep mat_id, formula, structure, imag, lambda, wlog, w2av and Tc at mu*=0.10/0.13 for each smearing. Remove duplicates against the 8,203 agm IDs already held. Join E_hull from the Alexandria PBEsol convex hull file (data/pbesol/convex_hull_ps_2023.12.29.json.bz2). Rank by Tc against E_hull and send only low-hull, dynamically stable entries to DFPT; leave out Li2AgH6 and Li2AuH6, given the kinetic-instability result.

checks.name: Bercx et al. MC3D BCS screening: 4,533-metal Allen-Dynes tier (beyond the 949 EPW subset)
checks.url_checked: https://archive.materialscloud.org/record/2593 (now 404); https://doi.org/10.24435/materialscloud:c8-gs, which redirects to records/0wv1s-yqg46 (v1, 2025-03-13, oai 2593, mcid 2025.39); API records 0wv1s-yqg46 and 0kqen-w8h90 (latest v4, DOI 10.24435/materialscloud:x2-ap, 2025-11-04) and the version list; README.md, files_description.md and Table_A to D.csv of v1 and v4, downloaded (each under 1 MB); OpenAlex record for 10.1103/sb28-fjc9; arXiv 2503.10943v2 including SI pages (alphaXiv)
checks.access_verified: [Certain] The record is open and the API and file downloads work with curl (WebFetch fails on DNS). There are four versions: c8-gs (v1), z3-he (v2), 9w-az (v3) and x2-ap (v4, latest). The record/2593 URL in the entry no longer resolves; use the DOI instead.
checks.license_verified: [Certain] Every version is CC BY 4.0 according to the record rights field. The PRX Energy article is CC BY.
checks.size_verified: [Certain] v1 holds super-screening.aiida at 18,759,651,337 bytes (17.47 GiB, matching the entry's 17.5 GiB), about 19.1 GiB in total. v4 holds QE-screening.aiida (14.99 GB) and EPW-screening.aiida (8.41 GB) plus extras, about 23.5 GiB in total. [Certain] Row counts: Table A 10,195, Table B 4,533, Table C 1,599, Table D 949. The only columns are Formula, Spacegroup, Source Database, Source ID and (v4) MC3D link. The tables contain no Tc, lambda or omega_log. The numeric Allen-Dynes values for the 4,533 metals exist only inside the AiiDA archive, in the groups paper/workchains/elph/q0.7, q0.5 and q0.3.
checks.label_quality: Calculated. The screening tiers used QE DFPT with SSSP pseudopotentials at q-distances of 0.7, 0.5 and 0.3 per angstrom and Allen-Dynes Tc at mu*=0.13. The top set was then recomputed in EPW with PseudoDojo. The entry has one error: the 949 only entered the EPW pipeline; they did not all get full Eliashberg treatment. 47 turned out magnetic, 347 failed, 270 were dynamically unstable and 33 had poor interpolation, which leaves 252 and then 250 with isotropic Migdal-Eliashberg Tc. Of the 144 with isotropic Tc above 5 K, 140 have anisotropic Tc. (v1 gave 240 and 110.) The coarse tier is noisy: MgB2 coarse Allen-Dynes 25.6 K against 12.3 K on fine grids, and RuO2 anisotropic 34 K against a measured value below 0.3 K.
checks.hpc_candidate: All structures are experimentally known (MC3D CIFs, with full positions in SI section 7), and all values are calculated with QE+EPW (PBEsol, harmonic) at mu*=0.13. (1) BaB2 (P6/mmm): pristine has a soft mode at H; hole doping of 0.065 holes per cell stabilises it. Then lambda 1.39, Tc 21.4 K (fine-grid Allen-Dynes), 33.0 K (isotropic), 61.6 K (anisotropic). [Likely] No synthesis of the doped phase or Tc measurement was found. (2) W2N3 (194): anisotropic 33.7 K. (3) TaRu3C (Pm-3m, icsd-77392): lambda 1.77, 16.5 K (Allen-Dynes), 21.0 K (isotropic), 25.0 K (anisotropic). It may be magnetic under PBE+U, and the perovskite is reported stable only at high temperature as TaRu3C0.5. (4) ZrRuSb (F-43m): anisotropic 13.2 K in the table, 11.1 K when recomputed; it sits near a van Hove singularity, so the Tc is sensitive to doping. No E_hull is given, but these are known phases. The project already parsed all 250 of these values from the SI (docs/bercx-published-check.md). None is close to room temperature.
checks.why: The source is real and open, and the 4,533-metal tier exists. The entry overstates what is new, for three reasons. First, the public CSVs carry no Tc values; they only list which compounds reached each stage. Second, the project already downloaded Tables A to D (sha256 recorded in docs/bercx-published-check.md), parsed the 250 SI results and uses the Table C 'Tc > 1 K' flag in physics-proxy2. Third, the 949 did not all get anisotropic Eliashberg treatment. The only data the project lacks is the graded coarse Allen-Dynes Tc and lambda for all 4,533 metals, which sits inside a 15 GB AiiDA archive and is noisy at the coarse tier. The highest prediction is about 62 K, and only for hole-doped BaB2.
checks.next_step: The tables need no action. If a graded calculated label for the 4,533 metals is wanted instead of the binary Table C flag, the owner would need to approve downloading QE-screening.aiida (about 15 GB) and exporting the q0.7/q0.5 ElectronPhononWorkChain outputs with aiida-core; otherwise drop it. Small fix: docs/bercx-published-check.md cites 10.24435/materialscloud:n9-a7 [Likely the concept DOI]. Record the version DOI used (c8-gs is v1, x2-ap is the latest), because the tables changed columns between versions.

By pressure in the file names: 0 GPa 157, 100 GPa 186, 200 GPa 187, 300 GPa 188, 500 GPa 181, 250 GPa 25, 50 GPa 8, and 21 with no pressure tag. 124 of the 0 GPa rows come from JARVIS and 33 from literature structures. checks.label_quality: All values are calculated, none measured. Method: QE DFPT, PBEsol, GBRV pseudopotentials, Gaussian-broadening interpolation, harmonic, non-spin-polarized, McMillan-Allen-Dynes with mu*=0.1. The 0.05 Ry broadening was confirmed for the 2D work [Certain]. Hydride: 2x2x2 q-grid and 45 Ry cutoff [Certain]. 2D: q-grids from 2x2x1 upward, denser for the Table 1 materials. The k and q columns of Table S2 appear swapped [Likely]. Known problems: (1) [Certain] Table S2 of the hydride paper lists 30 structures that have a PBEsol band gap yet a finite Tc. At 0 GPa these include NaH6 (53 K, gap 0.5 eV), MgH13 (27 K) and BaH3 (11 K). NaH6 at 0 GPa also appears in Table S1 as a stable superconductor (53 K and 50 K, Eform +0.2 eV/atom), which is an internal conflict. (2) [Certain] The top 0 GPa rows are high-pressure phases decompressed to 0 GPa with positive formation energy, for example Na2H11 at 113 K with Eform +0.3 eV/atom. They are not realistic ambient materials. (3) [Certain] The benchmark JSON gives no stability flag, so unstable or gapped rows cannot be filtered without the 25270012 record. (4) [Certain] The authors say McMillan-Allen-Dynes underestimates Tc at large lambda: their H3S is 154 K at 200 GPa, against 203 K measured.
checks.hpc_candidate: KAlH3, cubic perovskite Pm-3m (JVASP-93261, from MP mp-1097006). [Certain] Calculated Tc is 52 K at 0 GPa: QE DFPT, PBEsol/GBRV, 2x2x2 q-grid, harmonic, McMillan-Allen-Dynes, mu*=0.1 (Wines & Choudhary, Mater. Futures 3, 025602, 2024). The paper calls it dynamically stable, gives Eform -0.1 eV/atom (-0.111 in JARVIS) and says the gap opens and Tc is quenched above 100 GPa. [Likely] It is metastable: mp-1097006 is missing from the project's MP snapshot, which keeps phases up to 0.1 eV/atom above the hull. The snapshot shows KAlH4 (Pnma) and K3AlH6 on the K-Al-H hull, so Ehull is probably above 0.1 eV/atom. The JARVIS ehull field is empty. [Likely] It has never been synthesized; I found no experimental report. [Likely] A separate prediction, Du et al., Adv. Sci. 11, 2408370 (2024), is cited as giving 52-96 K at 0-7 GPa for KAlH3. I did not open it. [Certain] The structure is fully published: Pm-3m, a = 3.98 Angstrom, Al 1a (0,0,0), H 3d, K 1b (1/2,1/2,1/2). It has 5 atoms, so a converged DFPT check with a dense q-grid, plus an anharmonic or ZPE check given the light H, would be cheap. Not a candidate: elemental H at 0 GPa (43.5 K) and the high-pressure binaries decompressed to 0 GPa.
checks.why: The bulk 1,058 file is already held. Only the 2D monolayers and the hydride-pressure set are new. The 2D compositions are monolayers, so they do not map onto the project's bulk composition labels. Four-fifths of the hydride set is at 100-500 GPa, which is irrelevant to an ambient-pressure ranking. The roughly 157 rows at 0 GPa are low-fidelity (2x2x2 q-grid, McMillan formula) and contain gapped and positive-Eform rows that would need the separate 25270012 record to filter. They are poor ranking labels, but they surface one cheap, fully specified ambient hydride candidate (KAlH3). Two details of the original entry are wrong: the hydride set is not part of figshare 21370572 v4, and the 2D file is labelled 161 entries, not 165.
checks.next_step: Ask the owner to allow figshare.com in the session network, then fetch jarvis_epc_data_2d.json.zip (under 1 MB) and the hydride record 10.6084/m9.figshare.25270012. Check that each is under 20 MB first. Keep only 0 GPa hydride rows that have negative Eform, a PBEsol gap of 0, no imaginary modes and composition coverage. Add KAlH3 Pm-3m to the HPC shortlist as a converged recheck: denser k, 4x4x4 or 6x6x6 q, an Eliashberg solution, and a hull check against KAlH4 + K3AlH6 + Al. Read Du et al. 2024 first for its stability and Tc numbers.

checks.why: Local check (read-only): SuperCon2 v22.12.03 has 0 La3Ni2O7 rows (it predates the 2023 discovery), and the NIMS 2024 file has 0 Ni2O7 rows. The NEMAD Ni file has 56 Ni2O7/Ni3O10 rows, mostly bulk samples under pressure. No Ko or Zhou ambient-pressure film rows with a Tc are there. So the film results are new to the project, but as composition-only positives they would contradict the bulk ambient negatives for the same formula. Side finding [Likely, needs a check in the pipeline]: some NEMAD rows give a Tc of about 80 K for La3Ni2O7 and La2.7Nd0.3Ni2O7 (DOI 10.1103/PhysRevB.110.L100507, marked Experimental=True) and 20-30 K for La4Ni3O10, with the pressure field empty. Any pipeline that treats an empty pressure field as ambient would turn these pressure-only superconductors into false ambient positives.
checks.next_step: Do not add the films as composition-only positives. At most, keep them as annotated rows (substrate, strain, film thickness, onset vs zero-resistance Tc) that the ranking excludes. Check how the training build treats NEMAD Ni2O7/Ni3O10 rows with no pressure value, and mark them as high-pressure unless they already are. Calculated Tc 37 K, lambda 1.11-1.27, with Quantum ESPRESSO DFPT at the Gamma point only, LDA, Allen-Dynes McMillan formula with mu* = 0.12, harmonic. With the lowest mode removed it gives 27-28 K. A 2x2x2 q-grid check on B8C56 gave 24 K, and an imaginary acoustic branch appeared at 12.5 at% B. The atomic coordinates are said to be in the Supplemental Material (I have not seen them); this is an amorphous model, not a crystal CIF. It is metastable by construction, no energy above hull is reported, and the measured counterpart is the 36 K, 17 at% B sample. (2) Li et al., JPCC 129, 18831 (2025): first-principles Tc of 59 K at ambient for B-doped Q-carbon; method, structure and stability unverified (closed access). (3) The 2026 paper describes its QB33/QB50 structures only qualitatively (boron replacing the central carbon in randomly packed tetrahedra); I found no published coordinates. Crystalline B-C clathrates are a better use of DFPT time than amorphous Q-carbon.

Written as B-C formulas, they would also sit next to B4C and B-doped diamond rows and could teach the model a false B-C trend. The 2026 164-187 K claim is relevant to the room-temperature goal only if someone else reproduces it.
